Advances in network performance techniques are increasingly critical to 
improving communication reliability across modern confectionery business 
environments. As manufacturers integrate digital tools including ERP, MES, 
SCADA systems, smart sensors, industrial IoT devices, and cloud-based platforms 
the demand for stable, high-speed, and resilient communication infrastructures 
has intensified. This abstract presents an overview of emerging network 
technologies and optimization strategies that enhance operational efficiency, data 
integrity, and real-time responsiveness in confectionery production and 
enterprise workflows. Keywords: network performance, communication 
reliability, confectionery manufacturing, IoT, SDN, QoS, edge computing, cyber-
physical systems. Contemporary confectionery operations rely on seamless data 
exchange among interconnected production lines, automated dosing systems, 
temperature-controlled processes, and quality-monitoring platforms. Network 
performance techniques such as Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and 
Quality-of-Service (QoS) frameworks allow dynamic traffic prioritization, 
ensuring that time-sensitive control signals such as those used in moulding, 
enrobing, and packaging are delivered without delays or packet loss. High-speed 
industrial Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6/6E, and private 5G networks further strengthen 
communication stability by increasing bandwidth, reducing latency, and 
supporting dense device connectivity on factory floors and across supply-chain 
nodes. Edge computing is emerging as a cornerstone of communication 
reliability, enabling local processing of production data, predictive maintenance 
insights, and anomaly-detection algorithms without relying entirely on cloud 
infrastructures. This reduces communication bottlenecks and enhances system 
responsiveness in environments where continuous monitoring of thermal

Introduction 
The confectionery industry is undergoing rapid 
digitalization, driven by the need for greater 
operational precision, faster product cycles, enhanced 
traceability, and improved responsiveness to market 
demands (Ayanbode et al., 2024; Faiz et al., 2024). As 
confectionery 
enterprises 
modernize 
their 
manufacturing and business environments, digital 
systems now underpin nearly every operational layer 
from automated cooking and tempering lines to 
enterprise resource planning (ERP) platforms and 
cloud-enabled supply-chain systems (Aderonmu and 
Ajayi, 2024; Akerele et al., 2024). This transition 
marks a shift from conventionally manual or semi-
automated 
processes 
to 
highly 
interconnected 
environments where data flows continuously across 
production floors, warehouses, logistics networks, and 
corporate decision-making structures. The success of 
this transformation depends heavily on the reliability 
and performance of underlying communication 
networks, which function as the nervous system of 
the digital confectionery enterprise (Adebayo et al., 
2024; Abdul-Azeez et al., 2024). 
Reliable communication networks are essential for 
ensuring smooth interaction among production 
systems, real-time monitoring devices, inventory-
tracking platforms, and external partner interfaces 
(Obuse et al., 2024; Taiwo and Akinbode, 2024). 
Within the production environment, machine-to-
machine (M2M) coordination enables automated 
moulding, enrobing, packaging, and quality-control 
processes to operate with consistent accuracy. Any 
delay, packet loss, or network failure can disrupt 
temperature control, ingredient dosing, or packaging 
synchronization potentially leading to reduced quality 
or halted production (Uddoh et al., 2024; Fasawe et al., 
2024). Beyond the factory floor, efficient supply-chain 
communication is critical for coordinating raw-
material flows, maintaining compliance with food-
safety traceability regulations, and ensuring timely 
product distribution. At the enterprise level, seamless 
communication 
supports 
data-driven 
planning, 
predictive 
analytics, 
and 
cross-departmental 
collaboration (Rukh et al., 2024; Arowogbadamu et al., 
2024). Thus, communication reliability is no longer 
merely an IT concern; it is a strategic enabler of 
competitiveness and operational excellence. 
However, achieving high network reliability in 
modern confectionery environments is increasingly 
challenging. The proliferation of data-intensive digital

These innovations allow confectionery enterprises to

This review explores these advanced network

highlights how robust communication infrastructures 
can support the next generation of smart, automated, 
and data-driven confectionery enterprises. 
 
METHODOLOGY 
The review followed the PRISMA methodology to 
ensure a systematic, transparent, and rigorous 
evaluation of literature on advances in network 
performance techniques improving communication 
reliability in confectionery business environments. 
The process began with the identification phase, 
during which multiple academic and industrial 
databases including IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, 
SpringerLink, and Google Scholar were searched 
using keywords such as network performance, 
communication 
reliability, 
industrial 
IoT, 
confectionery 
manufacturing, 
SDN, 
QoS, 
edge 
computing, and industrial networking. Additional 
grey literature, including industry reports, technical 
standards, and white papers from automation and 
food-technology organizations, was also included to 
capture current industrial practices. 
In the screening phase, duplicate records were 
removed, and remaining studies were assessed based 
on titles and abstracts. Articles were excluded if they 
were unrelated to food manufacturing, lacked 
relevance to networking technologies, or focused 
solely on consumer-level communication systems. 
Studies 
emphasizing 
general 
manufacturing 
environments were retained if they presented 
applicable insights for confectionery contexts. The 
eligibility phase involved a full-text assessment of 
shortlisted papers to ensure alignment with the 
review 
scope, 
specifically 
addressing 
network 
performance optimization, industrial communication 
infrastructures, reliability improvements, and digital 
transformation in food processing. 
The final inclusion phase yielded a curated set of 
peer-reviewed articles, technical standards, case 
studies, and industrial guidelines that collectively 
informed the synthesis. Data extracted from the 
selected sources focused on core themes, including

2.1 Evolution of Networking in Confectionery 
Operations 
The evolution of networking in confectionery 
operations reflects the broader digital transformation 
taking place across the global food manufacturing 
sector. Historically, confectionery production relied 
on standalone machinery mixers, cookers, moulders, 
enrobers, and packaging units which operated 
independently with limited electronic control or data 
exchange. 
These 
early 
systems 
were 
largely 
mechanical, with human operators responsible for 
coordinating process timing, managing quality checks, 
and synchronizing production sequences. Over time, 
rising 
demand 
for 
product 
consistency, 
rapid 
throughput, and regulatory compliance drove the 
need 
for 
more 
integrated 
and 
intelligent 
communication systems (Akinlade et al., 2023; 
Akinbode et al., 2023). This shift marks the beginning 
of 
a 
progressive 
transformation 
from 
isolated 
equipment toward highly connected operational 
technology (OT) and information technology (IT) 
infrastructures. 
The integration of OT and IT represents one of the 
most significant stages in networking evolution 
within the confectionery industry. As programmable 
logic controllers (PLCs) and industrial control units 
became widespread, individual machines gained the 
capability to exchange basic signals and operational 
parameters. 
This 
laid 
the 
foundation 
for 
interconnected production lines where equipment 
could operate with coordinated timing and adaptive 
responses to production conditions. The expansion of 
industrial Ethernet, fieldbus systems, and wireless 
industrial communication enabled machines to 
communicate 
more 
effectively, 
supporting 
synchronized 
moulding, 
continuous 
cooking, 
automated 
cooling 
tunnels, 
and 
multistation 
packaging 
operations. OT–IT 
convergence 
also 
opened pathways for enterprise systems to access live 
production 
data, 
thus 
improving 
planning, 
maintenance scheduling, and resource allocation. 
The rise of real-time monitoring tools further 
accelerated 
networking 
advancement 
in 
confectionery operations. Supervisory Control and 
Data 
Acquisition 
(SCADA) 
systems 
enabled 
centralized visualization and control of temperature 
profiles, sugar crystallization, humidity conditions, 
and conveyor speeds. Manufacturing Execution 
Systems (MES) expanded this capability by linking 
production events with scheduling, batch tracking, 
and performance analytics. Automated quality-
control systems such as vision inspection, weight 
sensors, and inline texture analyzers introduced 
continuous data streams requiring reliable and high-
bandwidth connectivity (Sanusi et al., 2023; Didi et al., 
2023). These technologies transformed the factory 
floor into a data-rich environment where monitoring, 
decision-making, and process corrections occur in real 
time. Networking thus evolved from a supporting 
function to a core enabler of process reliability and 
product quality. 
Another major milestone in the evolution of 
confectionery networking was the adoption of cloud 
services and distributed digital platforms. Cloud-based 
MES, ERP, and supply-chain management systems

2.2 Core Network Performance Techniques 
Enhancing 
network 
performance 
has 
become 
essential for ensuring communication reliability 
across confectionery business environments. As 
production systems, supply-chain platforms, and 
enterprise 
applications 
become 
increasingly 
interconnected, robust communication infrastructures 
are required to support real-time monitoring, 
automated processes, and data-driven decision-
making. Several network performance techniques 
play a vital role in meeting these demands by 
optimizing traffic flow, improving connectivity, 
establishing redundancy, and enabling continuous 
monitoring (Faiz et al., 2024; Balogun et al., 2024) . 
Together, these strategies strengthen operational 
resilience and minimize disruptions in digitally 
advanced confectionery operations. 
Network optimization and traffic management are 
foundational to achieving reliable communication 
across fast-paced manufacturing lines. Software-
Defined Networking (SDN) has emerged as a pivotal 
technology, enabling centralized and programmable 
control over data routing. By decoupling the control 
and data planes, SDN allows dynamic traffic routing 
based on real-time production demands, bandwidth 
usage, and network conditions. This agility is crucial 
for confectionery environments where sensor data, 
control signals, and machine feedback must be 
transmitted without delay to maintain consistent

(Bayeroju et al., 2023; Sanusi et al., 2023). 
Complementing 
SDN, 
Quality-of-Service 
(QoS) 
mechanisms 
assign 
priority 
levels 
to 
critical 
communication flows. For example, time-sensitive 
control signals from PLCs regulating temperature, 
viscosity, or conveyor speeds receive priority over 
non-essential enterprise traffic. Load balancing 
further enhances network stability by distributing 
communication tasks across multiple channels, 
preventing bottlenecks and ensuring uninterrupted 
data flow even during peak production periods. 
Enhanced connectivity solutions form the second 
major pillar of network performance improvement. 
Industrial Ethernet and high-speed fibre networks 
provide 
the 
backbone 
for 
reliable 
wired 
communication on factory floors. These durable, 
interference-resistant 
systems 
support 
high-
bandwidth data transfer from SCADA systems, MES 
platforms, and automated quality-control devices. 
Wireless connectivity is equally important as smart 
sensors, mobile devices, automated guided vehicles 
(AGVs), and remote diagnostic tools proliferate in 
confectionery plants. Wi-Fi 6/6E offers improved 
throughput, higher device capacity, and lower latency 
compared to earlier wireless standards, enabling 
efficient 
communication 
in 
densely 
populated 
industrial settings. Private 5G networks extend these 
benefits by offering ultra-low latency, enhanced 
coverage, and secure dedicated bandwidth ideal for 
supporting mobile robots, edge devices, and large-
scale 
sensor 
deployments. 
Edge 
computing 
complements these connectivity solutions by enabling 
localized data processing, reducing cloud dependence, 
and minimizing latency. This is particularly valuable 
for real-time tasks such as anomaly detection, 
ingredient dosing control, or thermal monitoring, 
where milliseconds can influence product quality 
(Faiz et al., 2024; Chukwurah et al., 2024). 
Redundancy and failover mechanisms are essential 
components for ensuring continuous communication 
in mission-critical confectionery operations. Dual-
path routing provides an automatic switch to a 
secondary communication route if the primary 
pathway fails, preserving real-time control for heating 
units, moulding machines, and packaging lines. High-
availability (HA) cluster configurations are especially 
important for SCADA servers, MES databases, and 
communication controllers, enabling seamless failover 
without operational disruption. Redundant gateways, 
switches, 
and 
communication 
servers 
further 
strengthen resilience by eliminating single points of 
failure. 
These 
redundancy 
strategies 
minimize 
downtime risks, prevent production halts, and 
safeguard product integrity, especially in continuous 
processes such as chocolate tempering or sugar 
cooking where interruptions can cause material loss 
or equipment damage (Abayomi et al., 2022; Evans-
Uzosike et al., 2022). 
Real-time monitoring and diagnostics complete the 
framework of network performance techniques by 
ensuring proactive detection and resolution of issues. 
Advanced network analytics platforms continuously 
evaluate 
metrics 
such 
as 
latency, 
bandwidth 
utilization, packet loss, and device connectivity. AI- 
and ML-supported diagnostic tools identify patterns 
that indicate emerging failures, enabling predictive 
maintenance 
for 
network 
hardware 
and 
communication links. For instance, early detection of 
packet loss or jitter can prevent delays in machinery 
coordination or data corruption in quality-monitoring 
systems. 
Automated 
alerts 
notify 
network 
administrators and production supervisors when 
anomalies or cybersecurity threats arise, enabling 
immediate intervention to prevent disruptions or 
breaches (Chukwurah et al., 2024; Adebayo et al., 
2024). 
Collectively, 
these 
core 
network 
performance 
techniques 
traffic 
optimization, 
enhanced 
connectivity, redundancy systems, and real-time 
diagnostics provide a comprehensive foundation for 
ensuring communication reliability in confectionery

These

A 
primary

lies 
in 
improving 
synchronization 
between 
enterprise 
resource

high-speed 
confectionery 
lines

Enhanced network performance is also vital for 
maintaining reliable data flow in automated dosing, 
mixing, tempering, and packaging processes, which 
depend on precise, time-sensitive communication 
among distributed machines and digital controllers. 
Confectionery production involves narrow processing 
tolerances such as temperature profiles in chocolate 
tempering, viscosity control in syrups, or speed 
coordination between moulding and cooling tunnels 
making 
low-latency 
and 
high-availability 
communication 
essential.

mechanisms such as dual-path routing, high-
availability clusters, and redundant gateways ensure 
that network failures do not cascade into production 
stoppages. Coupled with AI-enabled predictive 
diagnostics 
and 
real-time 
monitoring 
tools, 
enterprises can detect early signs of congestion, failing 
network nodes, or unauthorized intrusions and 
intervene proactively. These capabilities translate into 
lower overall downtime, longer equipment lifespans, 
and improved operational predictability. For high-
volume confectionery producers, where margins 
depend on continuous processing and minimal 
wastage, such uptime optimization offers substantial 
competitive advantage. 
Another major benefit is the enhanced product 
traceability and regulatory compliance enabled by 
reliable, high-performance networks. Confectionery 
products are governed by stringent food safety 
regulations requiring detailed tracking of ingredients, 
batch 
histories, 
environmental 
conditions, 
and 
process 
parameters. 
Network 
performance 
improvements ensure that data generated by sensors, 
inspection systems, and MES platforms is captured, 
stored, and transmitted without corruption or delay. 
This 
supports 
end-to-end 
traceability 
across 
procurement, production, packaging, warehousing, 
and distribution. High-speed, resilient networks also 
enable the seamless integration of digital traceability 
tools like blockchain-based ledgers, cloud-based 
quality portals, and automated reporting dashboards 
used during audits. At the regulatory level, reliable 
data pathways ensure real-time monitoring of critical 
control 
points 
(CCPs), 
allergen 
management 
checkpoints, and sanitation cycles reducing the risk of 
compliance breaches, product recalls, or reputational 
damage (Simpson et al., 2024; Seyi-Lande and 
Onaolapo, 2024). 
Furthermore, 
advanced 
network 
performance 
techniques have a substantial impact on the 
strengthened cybersecurity posture of confectionery 
businesses. As production networks become more 
connected to vendors, remote engineers, cloud 
platforms, and IoT devices they also become more 
vulnerable to cyber threats such as ransomware, data 
interception, or OT system manipulation. Improved 
network 
architectures 
incorporating 
micro-
segmentation, encrypted communication channels, 
and continuous traffic monitoring mitigate these risks. 
AI-driven anomaly detection tools can quickly 
identify unusual traffic behaviours, unauthorized 
access 
attempts, 
or 
disruptions 
indicative 
of 
cyberattacks. Stable, optimized networks also support 
more secure remote maintenance and firmware 
updates, reducing the vulnerability surface associated 
with legacy equipment. By combining performance 
optimization with cybersecurity best practices, 
confectionery enterprises build a more resilient digital 
ecosystem capable of withstanding increasingly 
sophisticated cyber threats. 
The benefits and impacts of advanced network 
performance techniques extend beyond technological 
efficiency to influence organizational resilience, 
regulatory assurance, and strategic competitiveness. 
Increased communication reliability ensures stable 
production 
performance, 
reduced 
downtime 
safeguards business continuity, enhanced traceability 
strengthens compliance credibility, and improved 
cybersecurity protects both intellectual property and 
public trust. As confectionery enterprises continue to

2.5 Challenges 
Despite the significant advancements in network 
performance techniques and their transformative 
potential within confectionery business environments, 
several 
challenges 
constrain 
their 
widespread 
adoption and effective utilization. These challenges 
emerge from technological, economic, operational, 
and human-resource dimensions, reflecting the 
complexities 
of 
modernizing 
communication 
infrastructures in a traditionally machinery-intensive 
sector. 
As 
confectionery 
production 
becomes 
increasingly digitized and interconnected, resolving 
these issues becomes essential for enabling reliable, 
secure, and future-ready manufacturing operations. 
A major challenge stems from integration issues with 
legacy equipment and outdated cabling, which remain 
prevalent 
in 
many 
confectionery 
facilities. 
Historically, production lines were designed for 
mechanical automation with limited connectivity, 
relying on proprietary communication protocols and 
ageing wiring. Integrating these older systems with 
modern high-speed networks such as industrial 
Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6/6E, or private 5G poses substantial 
difficulties. Legacy programmable logic controllers 
(PLCs) and machinery may lack the interfaces 
required for real-time data exchange, while outdated 
cabling infrastructure cannot support high-bandwidth, 
low-latency communication. As a result, bridging 
OT–IT systems becomes complicated, requiring 
protocol converters, data gateways, or complete 
rewiring (Oloruntoba and Omolayo, 2024; Omolayo 
et al., 2024). These retrofit efforts often introduce 
interoperability 
issues, 
signal 
degradation, 
or 
inconsistent 
communication 
quality. 
For 
confectionery manufacturers with multiple product 
lines or geographically dispersed facilities, the 
integration burden is even more pronounced, 
delaying 
modernization 
and 
increasing 
implementation risks. 
Closely connected to these integration challenges is 
the high capital expenditure required for upgrading 
network 
infrastructure. 
Enhancing 
network 
performance involves investments in new cabling 
systems, industrial switches, hardened wireless access 
points, edge computing nodes, redundant servers, and 
advanced security appliances. For large manufacturers, 
the scale of upgrades across mixing, moulding, baking, 
cooling, and packaging areas can lead to substantial 
upfront costs. Small and medium-sized confectionery 
enterprises (SMEs), which dominate many regional 
markets, often lack the financial capacity for full-scale 
modernization. The return on investment (ROI) for 
network upgrades while beneficial in reducing 
downtime and improving productivity may take years 
to materialize, challenging decision-makers who must 
balance digital transformation priorities with budget 
constraints. Additionally, specialized installations 
require expensive engineering expertise and may 
necessitate planned production downtime, further 
increasing financial impact. 
Another major challenge involves the cybersecurity 
risks 
associated 
with 
increasingly 
connected 
environments. As confectionery operations expand 
their use of IoT devices, remote-access platforms, 
supplier-linked systems, and cloud-based analytics, 
they inadvertently broaden their attack surface. A 
compromised sensor, unsecured wireless endpoint, or 
misconfigured firewall can provide pathways for 
cyberattacks targeting proprietary recipes, batch-
quality data, supply-chain information, or production 
control systems. Threats such as ransomware, 
distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, or OT-
focused malware can disrupt operations, corrupt data, 
or halt production entirely. Many legacy machines 
lack 
built-in 
security 
features, 
making 
them

Cybersecurity risks necessitate layered defenses,

While advanced network performance techniques

of digital connectivity in the confectionery sector. 
2.6 Future Directions 
The continued evolution of network performance 
techniques in confectionery business environments 
will shape the next generation of digitally enabled, 
resilient, and intelligently coordinated operations. As 
factories become increasingly automated, horizontally 
integrated across supply chains, and vertically 
connected through ERP–MES–SCADA architectures, 
future advancements will focus on autonomy, ultra-
reliable communication, and secure data exchange. 
Several 
emerging 
directions 
spanning 
artificial 
intelligence, 
advanced 
wireless 
connectivity, 
blockchain, and predictive infrastructure will define 
how confectionery enterprises build and sustain high-
performance networks capable of supporting complex 
production 
ecosystems 
(Eyinade 
et 
al., 
2023; 
Ekwunife et al., 2024). 
One of the most transformative pathways involves the 
adoption 
of 
AI-driven 
autonomous 
network 
management. Traditional network administration in 
manufacturing settings relies on manual configuration, 
periodic monitoring, and reactive troubleshooting.

ecosystems expand, AI-enabled systems will assume a

stringent traceability requirements, and multi-party

improving transparency and trust. Distributed ledger 
technologies can support immutable tracking of raw 
materials such as cocoa, sugar, emulsifiers, and 
flavorings, ensuring authenticity, ethical sourcing, 
and compliance with food-safety regulations. In 
networked environments, blockchain-enabled smart 
contracts may automate procurement workflows, 
vendor approvals, and logistics scheduling with 
reduced risk of tampering or fraud. Furthermore,

transactions. This is particularly valuable for remote 
maintenance interactions, recipe data transfers, and

historical performance trends, network telemetry, and 
cyber-risk indicators to anticipate issues such as 
latency spikes, link failures, or unauthorized access

Conclusion 
Advanced network performance techniques play a 
foundational role in enhancing communication 
reliability across confectionery business environments, 
where digital systems, automated machinery, and 
data-driven 
coordination 
increasingly 
define 
operational success. As production facilities integrate 
ERP, MES, SCADA, and IIoT layers, the volume and 
criticality 
of 
exchanged 
information 
intensify. 
Techniques such as software-defined networking, 
industrial Ethernet, private 5G, edge computing, and 
real-time performance analytics collectively ensure 
low latency, consistent throughput, and secure data 
flow. 
These 
capabilities 
enable 
seamless 
synchronization among dosing systems, continuous 
processing equipment, packaging lines, and quality-
control platforms, thereby reducing disruptions and 
maintaining 
stable 
manufacturing 
performance. 
Reliable communication networks also strengthen 
supply-chain 
collaboration 
through 
timely 
information exchange with vendors, logistics partners, 
and 
distributors, 
reinforcing 
both 
operational 
accuracy and responsiveness. 
Continuous modernization of network infrastructure 
is essential to sustain the digital momentum of 
contemporary 
confectionery 
operations. 
As 
automation expands and smart devices proliferate, 
outdated or rigid communication architectures can 
become bottlenecks that limit technology adoption 
and compromise system integrity. Upgrading to 
advanced network performance techniques allows 
enterprises to accommodate higher data loads, support 
new automation technologies, and minimize the risks 
associated with legacy equipment and fragmented 
communication pathways. Routine enhancement also 
ensures alignment with cybersecurity expectations, 
reducing vulnerabilities introduced by increased 
interconnectivity. 
Strategically, resilient networks serve as the backbone 
for achieving efficiency, quality, and long-term 
competitiveness in the confectionery sector. High-
performing communication systems reduce downtime, 
enable predictive maintenance, support real-time 
quality assurance, and enhance traceability across 
production and distribution channels. They also 
facilitate faster decision-making and enable agile 
responses to market changes, regulatory requirements, 
and supply-chain uncertainties. By investing in robust, 
intelligent, and future-ready network infrastructures, 
confectionery enterprises position themselves to 
thrive in an increasingly automated, data-intensive, 
and digitally orchestrated manufacturing landscape.

Abstract: presents an overview of emerging network technologies and optimization strategies that enhance operational efficiency, data integrity, and real-time responsiveness in confectionery production and enterprise workflows. Keywords: network performance, communication reliability, confectionery manufacturing, IoT, SDN, QoS, edge computing, cyber- physical systems. Contemporary confectionery operations rely on seamless data exchange among interconnected production lines, automated dosing systems, temperature-controlled processes, and quality-monitoring platforms. Network performance techniques such as Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Quality-of-Service (QoS) frameworks allow dynamic traffic prioritization, ensuring that time-sensitive control signals such as those used in moulding, enrobing, and packaging are delivered without delays or packet loss. High-speed industrial Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6/6E, and private 5G networks further strengthen communication stability by increasing bandwidth, reducing latency, and supporting dense device connectivity on factory floors and across supply-chain nodes. Edge computing is emerging as a cornerstone of communication reliability, enabling local processing of production data, predictive maintenance insights, and anomaly-detection algorithms without relying entirely on cloud infrastructures. This reduces communication bottlenecks and enhances system responsiveness in environments where continuous monitoring of thermal Publication Issue Volume 11, Issue 5 September-October-2025 Page Number 430-447 Volume 11, Issue 5, September-October-2025 | http://ijsrcseit.com Nwankwo Constance Obiuto et al Int. Additionally, redundancy mechanisms such as failover routing, dual-path architectures, and high-availability clusters protect against network interruptions that could disrupt production continuity or compromise food-safety monitoring. Real-time network analytics and AI-driven diagnostics are transforming communication reliability by identifying performance degradation, cybersecurity threats, or hardware faults before they escalate. As confectionery enterprises expand their digital footprints, these network performance techniques collectively ensure robust operational communication, minimize downtime, and support traceable, high-quality product outputs. Ultimately, advanced, resilient network infrastructures form the backbone of competitive, data-driven, and customer- responsive confectionery business ecosystems.
